how: Tap Confirm on the beat to thrum the ground with your fork: steady taps bring the worms up, sloppy ones scare them down. Move the fork with the direction keys, because a patch that has given up its worms needs a rest. Birds are drawn to a messy rhythm, so Shoo them (Run) before they land. Charmed worms are counted and put back.

willaston.name: Willaston

rival.intro: Pat has a garden fork, a tin of patience and a technique that involves humming Abba at the soil.
rival.beaten: Pat looks at the plot, then at you, then writes down the words 'ask about the humming'.

willaston.real: The real thing is the World Worm Charming Championships at Willaston in Cheshire, held every summer. Each team gets a three-metre square plot and half an hour to bring worms to the surface by vibration, with no digging allowed. Every worm is counted, then put back where it came from.
